'''Michael Ashburner''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS|MAE}}<ref name=fellowofthers>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/michael-ashburner-11006/ |website=royalsociety.org |title=Professor Michael Ashburner FRS |publisher=[[Royal Society]] |location=London |author=Anon |year=1990 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151123162940/https://royalsociety.org/people/michael-ashburner-11006/ |archive-date=23 November 2015 }}</ref> (23 May 1942 – 7 July 2023) was an English [[biologist]] and Professor in the [[Department of Genetics, University of Cambridge|Department of Genetics]] at [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name=rubin>{{cite journal|first=
Gerald|last= Rubin |year=2023|title=Michael Ashburner (1942-2023) |journal =[[Current Biology]]|volume=33|issue=17|pages=R881–R883|doi= 10.1016/j.cub.2023.08.029|pmid=37619564|bibcode= 2023CBio...33R.881R |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gen.cam.ac.uk/research/ashburner.html |title=Emeritus Professor Michael Ashburner, Department of Genetics |publisher=University of Cambridge |website=gen.cam.ac.uk |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130115085846/http://www.gen.cam.ac.uk/research/ashburner.html |archive-date=15 January 2013 }}</ref> He also served as joint-head and co-founder of the [[European Bioinformatics Institute]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://library.cshl.edu/oralhistory/speaker/michael-ashburner/ |title=Cold Spring Harbor Laboratoty (CSHL) Oral History &#124; Michael Ashburner |archive-date=20 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320023155/http://library.cshl.edu/oralhistory/speaker/michael-ashburner/ }}</ref> of the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archives.wellcomelibrary.org/DServe/dserve.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqPos=0&dsqSearch=%28AltRefNo%3D%27pp%2Fmia%27%29 |title=iMichael Ashburner archive collection |website=wellcomelibrary.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150909054548/http://archives.wellcomelibrary.org/DServe/dserve.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqPos=0&dsqSearch=%28AltRefNo%3D%27pp%2Fmia%27%29 |archive-date=9 September 2015 }}</ref><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref> and a [[Fellow]] of [[Churchill College, Cambridge]].<ref>[https://archivesearch.lib.cam.ac.uk/repositories/9/resources/1405 The Papers of Michael Ashburner] held at [[Churchill Archives Centre]]</ref><ref name=inmemoriam>{{cite web|url=http://flybase.org/commentaries/2023_07/ashburner.html|website=flybase.org|publisher=[[FlyBase]]|year=2023|title=In Memoriam: Michael Ashburner|first1=Peter |last1=Cherbas|first2=
Thom|last2= Kaufman}}</ref>

==Education==
Born in [[Brighton]], [[Sussex, England]],<ref name=cell/>  Ashburner was educated at the [[Royal Grammar School, High Wycombe]] from 1953 to 1960.<ref name="whoswho"/> He studied the [[Natural Sciences (Cambridge)|Natural Sciences Tripos]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] as an undergraduate student of [[Churchill College, Cambridge]],<ref name="whoswho"/> receiving his [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in Genetics in 1964. His [[PhD]] was supervised by Alan Henderson<ref name="ashburnerphd">{{cite thesis|degree=PhD |first=Michael |last=Ashburner |title=Studies on puffing in the salivary gland chromosomes of Drosophila |publisher=University of Cambridge |date=1968|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.596176}} |website=cam.ac.uk |oclc=879391061 |url=https://idiscover.lib.cam.ac.uk/permalink/f/t9gok8/44CAM_ALMA21432627410003606 }}</ref><ref name=obit>{{cite web|url=https://www.gen.cam.ac.uk/department/history-of-the-department/michael-ashburner|website=cam.ac.uk|title=Professor Michael Ashburner FRS 1942 - 2023|author=Anon|year=2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721085713/https://www.gen.cam.ac.uk/department/history-of-the-department/michael-ashburner|archive-date=2023-07-21}}</ref> and awarded in 1968, followed by a [[Doctor of Science]] in 1978.<ref name="currentbio">{{Cite journal | last1 = Ashburner | first1 = M. | title = Michael Ashburner | doi = 10.1016/j.cub.2006.10.010 | journal = Current Biology | volume = 16 | issue = 22 | pages = R941–R943 | year = 2006 | s2cid = 29654933 | doi-access = free | bibcode = 2006CBio...16.R941A }}</ref>

}} {{open access}}</ref> Ashburner's career began in the early period of molecular biology prior to the development of most of the recombinant [[DNA]] techniques in use today, such as Northern/Southern/Western blotting.  Nevertheless, by observing patterns of "puffing" in [[polytene chromosomes]],<ref name="puffing"/> he established the existence of a cascade of genetic controls in the post-larval development triggered by [[ecdysone]].<ref name="ecdysone">{{Cite journal
| last1 = Hill | first1 = R. J.
| last2 = Billas | first2 = I. M. L.
| last3 = Bonneton | first3 = F. O.
| last4 = Graham | first4 = L. D.
| last5 = Lawrence | first5 = M. C.
| title = Ecdysone Receptors: From the Ashburner Model to Structural Biology*
| doi = 10.1146/annurev-ento-120811-153610
| journal = Annual Review of Entomology
| volume = 58
| pages = 251–271
| year = 2013
| issue = 1
| pmid = 23072463
| bibcode = 2013AREnt..58..251H
}}</ref> The Ashburner model of 1974 became a paradigm for [[metazoan]] gene regulation inasmuch as the [[François Jacob|Jacob]]-[[Jacques Monod|Monod]] model did for prokaryotes. Ashburner collaborated widely and mentored numerous PhD students and [[postdoctoral research]] students during his career.<ref name="collaborators">{{cite web|url=http://academictree.org/flytree/peopleinfo.php?pid=13863 |title=FlyTree - Michael Ashburner Details |archive-date=11 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111181320/http://academictree.org/flytree/peopleinfo.php?pid=13863 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|quote="Biologists would rather share their toothbrush than share a gene name"|doi=10.1038/35079694|title=Biology's name game: The confused nomenclature of genetics is blighting the field|first=Helen|last=Pearson|volume=411|pages=631–632|year=2001|issue=6838 |pmid=11395736 |s2cid=13625682 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

Ashburner was also a member of the consortium that eventually sequenced and annotated the ''[[Drosophila melanogaster]]'' genome.  Ashburner's recollections of the sequencing of the ''D. melanogaster'' genome forms the basis of a book entitled "Won for All: How the Drosophila Genome Was Sequenced".<ref name="wonforall">{{cite book |author=Michael Ashburner |title=Won for all: how the Drosophila genome was sequenced. |publisher=Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press |location=Plainview, N.Y |year=2006 |isbn=978-0-87969-802-7 |url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780879698027 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Sulston | first1 = John | author-link = John Sulston| title = All for All | doi = 10.1371/journal.pbio.0040198 | journal = [[PLOS Biology]] | volume = 4 | issue = 6 | article-number = e198 | year = 2006 | pmc =1475689 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref name="lablit">{{cite web |url=http://www.lablit.com/article/96 |title=Sequencing, sushi and sang-froid. Michael Ashburner's account of the fly genome project |access-date=2011-07-29 |first = Jennifer|last= Rohn | author-link = Jennifer Rohn|year = 2006}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Venter | first1 = J. C.|author-link1=Craig Venter | title = GENOMICS: An Ointment for the Fly | doi = 10.1126/science.1134998 | journal = Science | volume = 313 | issue = 5795 | page = 1892 | year = 2006 | s2cid = 82572658}}</ref> A prolonged effort by his laboratory to characterise the ''[[Alcohol dehydrogenase|Adh]]'' region<ref name="adhpaper"/> became invaluable for validating annotation strategies when large-scale genome information became available. Ashburner and his colleagues have received funding from the [[Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council|Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC)]], the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council (MRC)]]<ref name=gtr>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150416133500/http://gtr.rcuk.ac.uk/person/079A6C72-3F4B-43E4-919B-E01E3E695296|url=http://gtr.rcuk.ac.uk/person/079A6C72-3F4B-43E4-919B-E01E3E69529|title=UK Government Grants awarded to Michael Asburner|publisher=[[Research Councils UK]]|archive-date=2015-04-16 }}</ref> and [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC)]]<ref name=epsrc>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150416133811/http://gow.epsrc.ac.uk/NGBOViewPerson.aspx?PersonId=50745|url=http://gow.epsrc.ac.uk/NGBOViewPerson.aspx?PersonId=50745|title=EPSRC grants awarded to Michael Ashburner|archive-date=2015-04-16 |publisher=EPSRC}}</ref> for their studies on Drosophila genomics leveraging the ''D. melanogaster'' genome and its annotation.
[[File:Drosophila_melanogaster_Proboscis.jpg|right|thumb|200x200px|''Drosophila melanogaster'', the object of Ashburner's science]]

===Open science advocacy===
As part of his involvement the sequencing of the ''D. melanogaster'' genome, Ashburner played an instrumental role in ensuring that the resulting sequence and annotations would be made publicly available.<ref name="wonforall"/> Additionally, Ashburner made a strong case for the human genome published in [[Science (journal)|Science]] in 2000 by [[Celera Genomics]] to be made freely available,<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Marshall | first1 = E. | title = HUMAN GENOME: Storm Erupts over Terms for Publishing Celera's Sequence | doi = 10.1126/science.290.5499.2042 | journal = Science | volume = 290 | issue = 5499 | pages = 2042–2043 | year = 2000 | pmid =  11187813| s2cid = 37724876 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1016/S0140-6736(00)03531-5| title = Human genome row draws in journals| author=Anon|journal = [[The Lancet]]| volume = 357| issue = 9250| page = 81| year = 2001| s2cid = 5113446| doi-access = free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Moody|first=Glyn|title=Digital code of life: how bioinformatics is revolutionizing science, medicine, and business|year=2004|publisher=Wiley|location=Hoboken, NJ|isbn=978-0-471-32788-2|url=https://archive.org/details/digitalcodeoflif0000mood}}</ref><ref name="opendemocracy">{{cite web|last=Ashburner |first=Michael |title=Privatising our genes? |url=http://www.opendemocracy.net/theme_9-genes/article_407.jsp |access-date=8 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120114012025/http://www.opendemocracy.net/theme_9-genes/article_407.jsp |archive-date=14 January 2012 }}</ref> and spoke out repeatedly against the privatization of genomic resources.<ref name="opendemocracy"/><ref>{{cite web|last=Vince |first=Gaia |publisher=[[New Scientist]] |title=Fears over rice genome access |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn2061 |access-date=8 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110004415/http://www.newscientist.com/article/dn2061 |archive-date=10 January 2014 }}</ref> Ashburner was also one of the signatories of the first open letter to Science in 2001 calling for a centralized, open repository of the scientific literature,<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Roberts | first1 = R. J. | author-link1 = Richard J. Roberts| last2 = Varmus | first2 = H. E. | author-link2 = Harold E. Varmus| last3 = Ashburner | first3 = M. | author-link3 = Michael Ashburner| last4 = Brown | first4 = P. O. | author-link4 = Patrick O. Brown| last5 = Eisen | first5 = M. B. | author-link5 = Michael Eisen| last6 = Khosla | first6 = C. | author-link6 = Chaitan Khosla| last7 = Kirschner | first7 = M.| last8 = Nusse | first8 = R.| author-link8 = Roel Nusse| last9 = Scott | first9 = M. | title = Information Access: Building A ''GenBank'' of the Published Literature | doi = 10.1126/science.1060273 | journal = Science | volume = 291 | issue = 5512 | pages = 2318–9 | year = 2001 | pmid =  11269300| s2cid = 34395787 }}</ref> and subsequently became a strong advocate of [[Open Access]] publishing,<ref>{{YouTube|id=xPX8VcbcmOo|title="BioMed Central Author Video - Professor Michael Ashburner Part 2/3"}}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|id=FhV6uoROXKc|title="BioMed Central Author Video - Professor Michael Ashburner Part 3/3"}}</ref> speaking out for this cause in the scientific literature<ref name="currentbio"/><ref>{{YouTube|id=4Obpot5ER5o|title="BioMed Central Author Video - Professor Michael Ashburner Part 1/3"}}</ref> and popular media.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ward |first=Mark |title=Scientists threaten journal protest |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/1296750.stm |access-date=4 February 2012 |work=[[BBC News]] |date=26 April 2001 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070807211813/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sci/tech/1296750.stm |archive-date=7 August 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Meek|first=James|title=Science world in revolt at power of the journal owners|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2001/may/26/highereducation.physicalsciences|access-date=4 February 2012|location=London|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=29 May 2001}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Ward |first=Mark |title=Scientists call for online library |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/1516824.stm |access-date=4 February 2012 |work=[[BBC News]] |date=1 September 2001 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040701234843/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sci/tech/1516824.stm |archive-date=1 July 2004 }}</ref> He also provided written evidence to the UK Parliament Select Committee on Science and Technology supporting [[Open Access]] publishing<ref>{{cite web|last=Ashburner |first=Michael |title=UK Parliament Select Committee on Science and Technology APPENDIX 59 |url=https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm200304/cmselect/cmsctech/399/399we70.htm |access-date=4 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120715205507/http://www.publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm200304/cmselect/cmsctech/399/399we70.htm |archive-date=15 July 2012 }}</ref> and served on the initial advisory board of [[UK PubMed Central]],<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = McEntyre | first1 = J. ===Awards and honours===
Ashburner was elected a Foreign Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1993.<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780-2010: Chapter A |url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterA.pdf |publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |access-date=25 April 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110510021801/http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterA.pdf |archive-date=10 May 2011 }}</ref> He received the [[Gregor Mendel]] Medal from the Academy of Sciences, Czech Republic in 1998, the first George W. Beadle Award<ref name="beadle"/> of the [[Genetics Society of America]] in 1999, an honorary Doctorate from the [[University of Crete]] in 2002, an honorary Doctor of Science from the [[University of Edinburgh]] in 2003, the Genetics Society Medal of the UK Genetics Society in 2005 and the [[Benjamin Franklin Award (Bioinformatics)|Franklin Award of the Bioinformatics Organization]] in 2006. Ashburner was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1990|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1990]],<ref name=fellowofthers/><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Drysdale |first1=Rachel |last2=Russell |first2=Steve |date=2025 |title=Michael Ashburner. 23 May 1942—7 July 2023 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=78 |pages=27–48 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2024.0036 |doi-access=free }}</ref> his certificate of election reads:{{blockquote|text="Distinguished for his wide-ranging researches on the cytology, genetics and evolution of Drosophila melanogaster. He was the first to make a comprehensive map of puffs in the salivary gland polytene chromosomes and to define the stage at which each was expressed. He went on to demonstrate the effects of various stimuli, especially heat-shock and ecdysone, on puffing at specific loci, and correlated particular puffs with particular gene products. Combining genetic, cytological and molecular methodology, he has investigated in fine detail particular chromosome regions, especially that surrounding the Adh (alcohol dehydrogenase) gene, revealing many novel features of structure and function. He has also made important contributions to the understanding of evolution and speciation within the D.melanogaster group of species. Ashburner has unique standing as a scholar and authority in the whole area of Drosophila research."<ref name="royal">{{cite web |url=http://royalsociety.org |title=Certificate of election: Michael Ashburner. EC/1990/02 |publisher=The Royal Society |archive-date=8 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190708205647/https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=%28RefNo%3D%3D%27EC%2F1990%2F02%27%29 |location=London }}</ref>}}

Ashburner was awarded [[Member of the Academia Europaea]] (MAE) in 1989.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Ashburner_Michael|website=ae-info.org|title=Michael Ashburner MAE|publisher=[[Academia Europaea]]|author=Anon|year=1989}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ashburner married Francesca Ryan and had one son and two daughters, Rebecca, Geoffrey and Isabel.<ref name=obit/><ref name=whoswho/> He died on 7 July 2023, at the age of 81.<ref name=obit/><ref name=inmemoriam/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ebi_we-are-deeply-saddened-to-hear-about-the-activity-7083081386139471872-jIAH|website=linkedin.com|publisher=[[European Bioinformatics Institute]]|year=2023|first1=Ewan|last1=Birney|first2=Rolf|last2=Apweiler|author-link1=Ewan Birney|author-link2=Rolf Apweiler|title=We are deeply saddened to hear about the passing of our co-founder and former Head of Research, Michael Ashburner.}}</ref>
